prompt: Where does the sine wave come from?

current.title: Where the sine wave comes from

beats.say: Take an arm of length one, pinned at the centre of a circle.
Turn it a quarter of the way round, and watch how high its tip climbs.
Now let it go all the way round, and draw the height of the tip as it goes.
That height, traced against the angle, is the sine wave.
beats.show: The height of the tip is $\sin\theta$.
One turn of the circle is one period of the wave: $2\pi$.
